$comment: VENDORED COPY. asc-core-be owns this file at Contracts/active-time-quantities.v1.json; re-vendor it there rather than editing here. Everything below is that file's own comment, unchanged.
What an active-time figure is a measurement OF. This backend OWNS this file;
ai-engineer-tools and the app workspace vendor copies and pin them in their own
tests, the same arrangement as tool-telemetry-contract.v2.json.
It is a separate file from that one deliberately. That contract pins the
vocabularies a paired client may put on the wire at ingest. Nothing here is ever
sent by a client: these name what a COMPUTED figure reports. Same mechanism,
different ownership.
The prose definition is docs/ACTIVE_TIME.md, section 'The quantity is the label,
not the gap'. This file is the machine-readable half, and the one other repos
copy.
WHY THIS IS A SEPARATE AXIS FROM THE GAP. activeGapMinutes says how a figure was
cut; it does not say what was cut. Two figures sharing a gap can be incomparable
-- coverage and block_coverage are both cut at 30 here and answer different
questions. Two with different gaps can be legitimately compared: hands_on is cut
at 5 in ascenda-history-import and at 30 here, the same quantity on a different
corpus. So the gap is deliberately NOT part of the identity, or the guard would
forbid a comparison that is merely delicate.
AGENT-HOURS IS A QUANTITY, NOT A PRESENTATION. docs/ACTIVE_TIME.md says so twice
-- 'Both quantities are real; only the union is elapsed time' and 'A summed
figure may be reported as agent-hours, never as where a week went' -- but its
four-name table had no name for the summed form, so the two figures that most
needed telling apart were the two it could not describe. In ai-engineer-tools'
localHandoff.ts, HandoffProjectDigest.handsOnMinutes is summed across sessions
(4.2x wall clock on the reference machine) while ProjectElapsedActive.
handsOnMinutes is unioned: same spelling, one nesting level apart. Both
deliberate, both documented, nothing mechanical telling them apart.
WHAT THE GUARD FORBIDS, AND WHAT IT MUST NOT. Adding or subtracting across
quantities is a bug in the general case. Two exceptions are real and must stay
expressible:
- DIVISION across a concurrencyPair is exactly meanConcurrency, the honest
form of what a naive sum reports by accident. Never route it through the
comparability guard.
- The disjointHalves below sum to their whole BY CONSTRUCTION. SplitActiveMinutes
assigns each gap-split span entirely to one side, so hands_on and supervising
partition the same spans and their total is coverage, not a double count.
What is forbidden is RENDERING that total as attention -- 'you spent 22
minutes' collapses 5 of typing and 17 of an agent running -- which is a claim
about presentation, not about arithmetic. Earlier comments in this repo
conflated the two and said the addition itself was invalid; it is not.
Which quantities are elapsed time -- the union of underlying intervals, safe to
render as 'where your week went' -- and which are summed agent-hours. A surface
that quotes a summed figure as elapsed time is the defect this split prevents.

concurrencyPairs.$comment: summed / unioned is meanConcurrency for this pair. Division legal, addition not.

$comment: Partition the same spans, so their total is the whole and adding them is
legal. The summed pair (hands_on_agent_hours, supervising_agent_hours) is
disjoint for the same reason, but there is no declared name for its whole --
total agent-hours -- so the guard does not bless that addition. Add the name
before adding the pair, rather than letting an addition produce a figure no
quantity describes.
